instruction: Bulk Component Renaming via Regex The file `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\naming_mess.dae` is a COLLADA scene that came out of a SketchUp model where 50 components were named arbitrarily by several different modellers over the project's lifetime. The `<geometry>` elements in `library_geometries` therefore carry messy, inconsistent names like `chair_5`, `TABLE003`, `lamp-01`, `Desk_002`, `sofa 12`, `BookShelf_7`, `window-003`, etc. - a mix of capitalizations (lower, UPPER, Title, Mixed), separators (underscore, hyphen, space, none) and zero-padding styles (no padding, 2-digit, 3-digit). Your task is to normalize every component name to the canonical form <Type>_<NNN> where: * `<Type>` is the leading alphabetic prefix of the original name, Title-cased (first letter upper, rest lower). Non-alphabetic, non-numeric characters (spaces, hyphens, underscores) between the prefix and the number must be discarded. * `<NNN>` is the trailing integer run of the original name, zero-padded to 3 digits. Examples: * `chair_5` -> `Chair_005` * `TABLE003` -> `Table_003` * `lamp-01` -> `Lamp_001` * `Desk_002` -> `Desk_002` * `sofa 12` -> `Sofa_012` * `BookShelf_7`-> `Bookshelf_007` If two or more original names normalize to the same canonical string (e.g. both `chair_5` and `CHAIR_05` map to `Chair_005`), disambiguate by appending `_<k>` where `k` is a 1-based integer for the second, third,... collision (so the first occurrence keeps the clean form `Chair_005`, the second becomes `Chair_005_2`, the third `Chair_005_3`, and so on). Every output name must therefore match the regex ^[A-Z][a-z]+_\d{3}(_\d+)?$ Deliverables: 1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` - a COLLADA file with the same 50 `<geometry>` entries as the input, but with the `name` attribute of each `<geometry>` renamed to its canonical form. Preserve the mesh data; only the name changes. 2. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\rename_map.json` - a JSON object with exactly 50 key->value entries mapping each original (messy) name to its new (canonical) name. Exactly one entry per input geometry. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` parses as valid COLLADA via pycollada. 2. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` contains exactly 50 `<geometry>` entries. 3. Every `<geometry>` name in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae` matches the regex `^[A-Z][a-z]+_\d{3}(_\d+)?$`. 4. All 50 output names are unique. 5. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\rename_map.json` is valid JSON with exactly 50 keys. 6. The set of keys in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\rename_map.json` equals the set of original names in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\naming_mess.dae`. 7. The set of values in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\rename_map.json` equals the set of `<geometry>` names in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.dae`. 8. Each value in `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\rename_map.json` is the correct canonical form of its key (up to collision suffixes). [Software] Launch SketchUp with `C:\SketchUp 2026 26.0.429 x64 En Portable\SketchUp.exe` (adjust if your install differs).
